arxiv-2108-02268.title: Effects of mobility restrictions during COVID19 in Italy
arxiv-2108-02268.description: Abstract To reduce the spread and the effect of the COVID-19 global pandemic, non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) have been adopted on multiple occasions by governments. In particular lockdown policies, i.e., generalized mobility restrictions, have been employed to fight the first wave of the pandemic.

arxiv-2110-02106.title: Unified Theory of Characteristic Modes: Part II – Tracking, Losses, and FEM Evaluation Thanks: Manuscript received August 7, 2026; revised August 7, 2026. This work was supported by the Swedish Research Council (2017-04656) and Czech Science Foundation under project No. 21-19025M . Thanks: M. Gustaf
arxiv-2110-02106.creator: Mats Gustafsson, Lukas Jelinek
arxiv-2110-02106.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mats Gustafsson, Lukas Jelinek. This is the second component of a two-part paper dealing with a unification of characteristic mode decomposition. This second part addresses modal tracking and losses and presents several numerical examples for both surface- and volume-based method-of-moment formulations. A new tracking algorithm based on algebraic properties of the transition matrix is developed, achieving excellent precision and requiring a very low number of frequency samples as compared to procedures previously reported in the literature.

arxiv-2110-05392.title: Local Effects of Grid-Forming Converters Providing Frequency Regulation to Bulk Power Grids This work is supported by OSMOSE project. The project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 Research and Innovation Program under Grant 773406.
arxiv-2110-05392.creator: Antonio Zecchino, Francesco Gerini, Yihui Zuo, Rachid Cherkaoui, Mario Paolone, Elena Vagnoni
arxiv-2110-05392.description: Abstract The progressive displacing of conventional generation in favor of renewable energy sources requires restoring an adequate capacity of regulating power to ensure reliable operation of power systems. Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs) are considered to be promising assets to restore suitable frequency regulation capacity levels.

arxiv-2202-01013.title: Fairness of Machine Learning Algorithms in Demography
arxiv-2202-01013.creator: Ibe Chukwuemeka Emmanuel, Ekaterina Mitrofanova
arxiv-2202-01013.description: Abstract The paper is devoted to the study of the model fairness and process fairness of the Russian demographic dataset by making predictions of divorce of the 1st marriage, religiosity, 1st employment and completion of education. Our goal was to make classifiers more equitable by reducing their reliance on sensitive features while increasing or at least maintaining their accuracy.

arxiv-2202-02661.title: LiDAR dataset distillation within bayesian active learning framework Understanding the effect of data augmentation
arxiv-2202-02661.creator: Ngoc Phuong Anh Duong 1 , Alexandre Almin 1 Léo Lemarié 1 and B Ravi Kiran 1 1 Machine Learning, Navya, France { first_name.second_name } @navya.tech
arxiv-2202-02661.description: Abstract Autonomous driving (AD) datasets have progressively grown in size in the past few years to enable better deep representation learning. Active learning (AL) has re-gained attention recently to address reduction of annotation costs and dataset size. AL has remained relatively unexplored for AD datasets, especially on point cloud data from LiDARs.

arxiv-2308-15662.title: Sojourns of fractional Brownian motion queues: transient asymptotics
arxiv-2308-15662.creator: Krzysztof Dȩbicki, Enkelejd Hashorva, Peng Liu
arxiv-2308-15662.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Krzysztof Dȩbicki, Enkelejd Hashorva, Peng Liu. Abstract:
We study the asymptotics of sojourn time of the stationary
queueing process
Q(t),t\geq 0
fed by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter
H\in(0,1)

above a high threshold
u
. For the Brownian motion case
H=1/2
, we derive the exact asymptotics of

\mathbb{P}\left\{\int_{T_{1}}^{T_{2}}\mathbb{I}(Q(t)>u+h(u))dt>x\Big|Q(0)>u\right\}

as
u\to\infty
, where
T_{1},T_{2},x\geq 0
and
T_{2}-T_{1}>x
, whereas for all
H\in(0,1)
, we obtain sharp asymptotic approximations of

\mathbb{P}\left\{\frac{1}{v(u)}\int_{[T_{2}(u),T_{3}(u)]}\mathbb{I}(Q(t)>u+h(u))dt>y\Bigl\lvert\frac{1}{v(u)}\int_{[0,T_{1}(u)]}\mathbb{I}(Q(t)>u)dt>x\right\},\quad x,y>0

as
u\to\infty
, for appropriately chosen
T_{i}
’s and
v
.

arxiv-2402-08294.title: Learning semantic image quality for fetal ultrasound from noisy ranking annotation
arxiv-2402-08294.creator: Manxi Lin 1,∗ , Jakob Ambsdorf 2,4,∗ , Emilie Pi Fogtmann Sejer 3 , Zahra Bashir 3 , Chun Kit Wong 1,4 , Paraskevas Pegios 1,4 , Alberto Raheli 1 , Morten Bo Søndergaard Svendsen 2,3 , Mads Nielsen 2,4 , Martin Grønnebæk Tolsgaard, 3 , Anders Nymark Christensen 1 , Aasa Feragen 1,4
arxiv-2402-08294.description: Abstract We introduce the notion of semantic image quality for applications where image quality relies on semantic requirements. Working in fetal ultrasound, where ranking is challenging and annotations are noisy, we design a robust coarse-to-fine model that ranks images based on their semantic image quality and endow our predicted rankings with an uncertainty estimate.

arxiv-2412-12896.title: 3D Free-Form Optical Lens - Miniaturised Fibre Couplers for Astrophotonics
arxiv-2412-12896.creator: Haoran Mu 1,∗ , Daniel Smith 1,∗ , Tomas Katkus 1 , Nguyen Hoai An Le 1 , Dominyka Stonyte 2 , Darius Gailevičius 2 , Dan Kapsaskis 1 , Alexander Del Frate 1 , Talwinder Singh Bedi 3 , Donatas Narbutis 4 , Vijayakumar Anand 5 , Darija Astrauskyte 6 , Lina Grineviciute 6 , Soon Hock Ng 1 , Karl Glaze
arxiv-2412-12896.description: Abstract In astronomy, multi-object spectrographs employ fibre positioning robots to couple the light from multiple astronomy sources (stars or galaxies) into multiple multi-mode fibres, which are distributed across the focal plane of the telescope. These fibres transport the celestial light to the entrance slit of a spectrograph (or bank of spectrographs) for analysis.

arxiv-2509-25622.title: Layer-wise dynamic rank for compressing large language models
arxiv-2509-25622.creator: Zhendong Mi Stevens Institute of Technology zmi2@stevens.edu Bian Sun Carnegie Mellon University bians@alumni.cmu.edu and Grace Li Zhang Technical University of Darmstadt grace.zhang@tu-darmstadt.de Shaoyi Huang Stevens Institute of Technology shuang59@stevens.edu
arxiv-2509-25622.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have rapidly scaled in size, bringing severe memory and computational challenges that hinder their deployment. Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based compression has emerged as an appealing post-training compression technique for LLMs, yet most existing methods apply a uniform compression ratio across all layers, implicitly assuming homogeneous information included in various layers.

britannica-1911-templars.description: Article 'Templars' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Christ and of the Temple of Solomon (pauperes commilitones Christi templique Salomonici), formed one of the three great military orders, founded in the 12th century. Unlike the Hospitallers and the Teutonic Knights it was a military order from its very origin.

pmc-11435709.title: The Role of the N-Terminal Domain of Thrombomodulin and the Potential of Recombinant Human Thrombomodulin as a Therapeutic Intervention for Shiga Toxin-Induced Hemolytic-Uremic Syndrome
pmc-11435709.creator: Sarah Kröller, Jana Schober, Nadine Krieg, Sophie Dennhardt, Wiebke Pirschel, Michael Kiehntopf, Edward M Conway, Sina M Coldewey
pmc-11435709.description: Hemolytic-uremic syndrome (HUS) is a rare complication of an infection with Shiga toxin (Stx)-producing Escherichia coli (STEC-HUS), characterized by severe acute kidney injury, thrombocytopenia and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and specific therapy is still lacking. Thrombomodulin (TM) is a multi-domain transmembrane endothelial cell protein and its N-terminal domain has been implicated in the pathophysiology of some cases of HUS.

pmc-12418673.title: Mental well-being and work capacity: a cross-sectional study in a sample of the Swedish working population
pmc-12418673.creator: Agneta Blomberg, Gunnel Hensing, Monica Bertilsson, Carin Staland-Nyman, Christian Ståhl, Lisa Björk
pmc-12418673.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMental health problems are common in the working-age population. More knowledge is needed on how to support work participation and reduce sickness absence. The objective of the study was to estimate the distribution of mental well-being and work capacity in women and men in a working population and assess the association between mental well-being and work capacity, while adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, health status, and working positions.MethodsCross-sectional data were collected through an online survey distributed to individuals who were currently working.

pmc-12469800.title: The Links Between Physical Activity, Metacognition, and Empathy Among Physiotherapy Students
pmc-12469800.creator: Anica Kuzmić, Manuela Filipec, Miro Jakovljević, Freda N Gonot-Schoupinsky, Claude-Hélène Mayer
pmc-12469800.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background: Physical activity, metacognitive awareness, and empathy are interconnected factors that play a significant role in the overall well-being of university students. Together, these elements contribute to the development of more self-aware, emotionally intelligent, and academically engaged students. The aim of this study is to explore the relationship between physical activity, empathy, and metacognition among physiotherapy students, as well as determining whether differences exist between undergraduate and graduate students.

pmc-13207928.title: Beyond Reperfusion: Early Molecular Drivers and Therapeutic Opportunities in Acute Post-Infarction Cardiac Fibrosis
pmc-13207928.creator: Desaree Tan, Yi Ee Lye, Pranjal Patel, Nay Aung Minn, Anne Cao Le, Alex Bobik, Tin Kyaw
pmc-13207928.description: Heart failure is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, often developing as a consequence of acute myocardial infarction. Current management focuses on timely reperfusion via percutaneous coronary intervention. Yet, this approach fails to prevent the molecular cascades that drive the death of viable yet stressed cardiomyocytes within the infarct and peri-infarct zone.

pmc-13369754.creator: Kaya Molo, Ruken Ege, Kübra Ati̇k, Elif Çıtak, Orçun Çulcuoğlu, Hakan Darıcı, Emel Ordu
pmc-13369754.description: Infectious diseases exacerbate atherosclerosis-associated morbidity and mortality by inducing sustained inflammatory responses characterized by elevated IL-6, TNF-α, IFN-γ, and CXCL10. Persistent CXCL10-driven recruitment of CXCR3⁺ immune cells promotes endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerotic progression. Although mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) respond to inflammatory cues and secrete CXCL10, the contribution of CXCL10/CXCR3 signaling to intrinsic MSC immunomodulatory programming remains poorly understood.

pmc-13472827.creator: Rosie H. Whittle, Gregory S. Fraley, Colin G. Scanes, Sara K. Orlowski-Workman, Maricela A. Maqueda, Alexander H. Nelson, Zachary Grider, Shawna L. Weimer
pmc-13472827.description: IntroductionSustainable water use in poultry production is becoming pivotal. Extreme weather events and increased water scarcity may increase the risk of temporary disruptions in freshwater access. To address this challenge, the aim of this study was to determine how broilers selected for low (LWE) and high (HWE) water conversion efficiency responded to water deprivation.
